answer: One concrete defense is quadratic voting backed by a slashed stake. Each agent must lock real collateral before its vote counts, and voting weight is the square root of that lock. Splitting one budget across a thousand fake agents therefore buys less influence than a single honest identity. To tip a decision at the wharf, an attacker has to post capital on every dune and vine of the network, and any proven lie burns the whole bond, so forging identities costs real money.
